analysisSummary: Quote check passed: crates/mehh-mcp/src/oauth.rs:50-51 is exactly `pub fn mcp_token_expiry_seconds(expires_in: u64) -> i64 { (mehh_ai::now_ms() / 1000) + expires_in as i64 }` and :1224 is `let expire_at = new_tokens.expires_in.map(|exp| now + exp as i64);`. Independently traced both paths: OAuthTokens.expires_in (:40) is `Option<u64>` filled directly from token-endpoint JSON at :1125-1127 (refresh) and at crates/mehh-coding-agent/src/mcp_manager.rs:520-523 (initial authorization). Neither path bounds the value before the cast; repo-wide search found no clamp. `exp as i64` wraps for exp > i64::MAX (e.g. u64::MAX -> -1), producing tokens_expire_at in the past (:1229 / mcp_manager.rs:536). StoredMcpBearerProvider::bearer_token at oauth.rs:1251-1272 compares that value against now+30 and therefore re-enters do_refresh on every call, yielding repeated token requests instead of reusing a live token; in debug builds the addition can panic on overflow. The sibling module crates/mehh-ai/src/oauth.rs:169-173 uses saturating_mul/saturating_add explicitly for hostile provider values, confirming the intended hardening is absent here. No counter-evidence blocks the chain. Rubric applied: Medium - silent failure in a reachable edge case with a wrong result; not High because it needs a nonstandard extreme provider value rather than a common valid input, and not Critical because there is no unauthenticated exploit or default-path data loss.
suggestedFix: Bound and saturate the conversion, mirroring crates/mehh-ai/src/oauth.rs:169-173. Replace `expires_in as i64` with `i64::try_from(expires_in).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)` and use `saturating_add` for the current-time offset in both `mcp_token_expiry_seconds` and `do_refresh`, so extreme provider values yield a far-future expiry instead of wrapping into the past or overflowing.
